consent.consentTextSummary: Participant authorized use of answers as technical/historical testimony about CanalBarra.com, without publication of email or private data.

coreConfirmedClaims.claim: Lucas Nercessian remembers being with Raphael/BarMan when they entered Canal #Barra, found it without owner/operator, and Raphael/BarMan registered it on BRASnet.

Canal Barra began with a manual homepage, updated by Raphael/BarMan with pages and photos, and later evolved under the CanalBarra.com domain into a dynamic site with database, user registration and login/modify-cadastro area.
Lucas installed or configured the technical environment that enabled CanalBarra.com to operate dynamically, including ColdFusion and Microsoft Access.
Before the dynamic phase, the site was mainly a manual homepage updated by Raphael/BarMan; later it gained dynamic functions due to the technical structure installed/configured by Lucas.
Work/development experience in Los Angeles helped Lucas and Raphael/BarMan learn or consolidate technologies such as ColdFusion and Microsoft Access, later used in the evolution of CanalBarra.com.
After ColdFusion and Microsoft Access installation/configuration, CanalBarra.com supported user registration with photos and descriptions, serving as a people-connection tool.
coreConfirmedClaims.responseSummary: Cadastro de usuários com fotos e descritivo de cada um; ferramenta para conexão de pessoas; prévia do que foi Orkut e Facebook.

coreConfirmedClaims.claim: The dynamic phase of CanalBarra.com allowed user/nickname registration through the website itself.
CanalBarra.com had a login or modify-cadastro area allowing users to alter their own data.
Users could edit biography, personal description or profile information on the site.
Users could add, change or associate photos with their cadastro/profile on CanalBarra.com.
CanalBarra.com had a page or area with Canal #barra rules.
CanalBarra.com published events, parties, IRContros, meeting photos or social records linked to Canal #barra.
CanalBarra.com functioned as a web layer linked to the channel, rather than replacing IRC as the center of daily interaction.
coreConfirmedClaims.response: Funcionava como camada web ligada ao canal

coreConfirmedClaims.claim: Lucas describes Canal Barra not as merely an IRC channel, but as an ecosystem formed by IRC, website, registrations, photos, events, reputation and gatherings.
coreConfirmedClaims.response: Ecossistema IRC + site + cadastros + fotos + eventos + reputação + encontros

coreConfirmedClaims.claim: CanalBarra.com made relationships more personal through photos and meetings, doing something IRC alone did not do.
coreConfirmedClaims.response: Deixava a relação mais pessoal, com fotos e encontros.

coreConfirmedClaims.claim: CanalBarra.com materialized what were otherwise only IRC nicknames.
coreConfirmedClaims.response: Materializava o que eram apenas nicknames

coreConfirmedClaims.claim: Lucas describes the main function of CanalBarra.com inside the Canal #barra ecosystem as social interaction.

negativeOrLimitingClaims.claim: It would be exaggerated to say that CanalBarra.com made money or operated as a profitable commercial project.
negativeOrLimitingClaims.response: Que ele dava dinheiro. Porque não dava.
negativeOrLimitingClaims.interpretation: CanalBarra.com should be described as a social/community infrastructure, not as a profitable web business or commercial platform.

knownMaterialSupportContext.example: BarMan obtained an arrangement with Raul Pizzaria that reportedly provided two pizzas per month.
knownMaterialSupportContext.boundary: This may support the existence of limited material sponsorship or community support, but it must not be interpreted as proof that the website generated profit or meaningful revenue.

summaryForUseInThesis: Lucas Nercessian confirms that Canal Barra should not be reduced to IRC-only. According to his technical participant statement, Canal Barra evolved from a manual homepage updated by Raphael/BarMan into CanalBarra.com, a dynamic ColdFusion/Microsoft Access website whose environment he installed or configured. The dynamic site supported user/nickname cadastro, login/modify-cadastro, profile/biography information and photos, and published rules, events, IRContros and social records. Lucas characterizes Canal Barra as an ecosystem of IRC, site, cadastros, photos, events, reputation and gatherings, and states that CanalBarra.com materialized what were otherwise only nicknames. Lucas also explicitly limits monetization claims: it would be exaggerated to say that CanalBarra.com made money. At most, the archive currently records limited material support, such as the founder-reported Raul Pizzaria arrangement of two pizzas per month, not profit or meaningful revenue.
methodologicalNote: This record is a sanitized public metadata extraction from a private Google Forms CSV. The participant email and raw CSV are not published. Answers marked as 'Não lembro' are explicitly not used as corroboration. The timeline/feed-like answer is preserved as an ambiguity requiring technical clarification and should not be overclaimed. The monetization note is included to prevent commercial-platform overclaiming: limited sponsorship or in-kind support is not treated as profit.
